newsitem.title: BELGIUM: GENERALE BANK,GIMV IN LOANS FOR OPTION INTERNAT'L.
newsitem.headline: GENERALE BANK,GIMV IN LOANS FOR OPTION INTERNAT'L.

text.p: Generale Bank and Flemish investment company GIMV are lending Option International NV (Mobile Data Communications) 105 million Belgian francs, Generale Bank said in a statement on Monday.
The loan is convertible and subordinated.
GIMV, currently the main shareholder in Option, participates in the operation for 35 million francs, it said.
Generale Bank said an employee stock option plan was being worked out. Details were not available from the bank.

A spokesman for Generale Bank's Corporate Finance Department said he could not yet say how many shares in Option Generale Bank would hold if the loan were converted. "The conversion ratio has not been set yet," he said.

Asked whether the convertible loan was a precursor to a stock market listing, he said it was too early to discuss that. "(The loans) are a step in the development of the company's capital and certainly not the last step."
Turnover at Option, which employs 35 people, grew from 100 million in 1995 to 300 million in 1996 and had already reached the 300 million franc mark after the first six months of 1997.
The company made a small, unspecified profit in 1996 and "had already done particularly well" in the first half, the Generale Bank spokesman said.
Option makes credit card-size modems allowing data communication via land lines and GSM. Currently the company operates mainly in Belgium, but its products are licenced in two dozen countries.
The current capital increase is the second in just over a year. The previous increase of 15 million francs dates back to May 1996 and made GIMV the main shareholder.
GIMV then offered warrants to Option chief executive officer Jan Callewaert, which would soon enable him to become the majority shareholder again.
